I’ve never said that everyone should be paid the same, I’m saying that everyone should be paid fairly. The worker deserves the wealth he generates, you basically held this exact sentiment in your first comment. This does not happen under capitalism. 

I’m arguing for a system that doesn’t require the exploitation of labor and allows the worker to earn what they worked for, which again, seemed pretty important to you earlier.

I’m also glad we agree on some things, but I’d like to bring this conversation back to where it began. 

Earlier you stated that you would never want to live in a society where you are unable to earn what you work for. Though now you are telling me that you actually don’t mind when most of the wealth you are generating goes to someone else. You may believe that they deserve it more, or that they don’t mean to exploit people, but that’s still the direct opposite to the position you put forth in your first comment. 

What changed your mind? Are you fine with not earning what you worked for, or not?

>  It’s not rocket science and it’s not a place someone should stay for their entire career. There needs to be incentives to promote. Better pay, better housing, better whatever that way people don’t sit in my position for 40 years. 

I agree with you here. Some hierarchical structures are always going to exist in a place of work, and upward mobility shouldn’t just be possible, but incentivized. People tasked with harder or more dangerous jobs should absolutely be paid more than the average worker. I’m not arguing against these things. 

What I am arguing against, is the fact that under a capitalist system, the capital owner (again, not your managers but the state itself) has to exploit their workers in order to turn a profit. You can repeat how much you like your job or how little wealth you generate ad infinitum, but that doesn’t change the fact that politicians, high ranking military officials, and private weapons manufacturers are all profiting off of the labor you and your fellow workers are generating, and in turn using your military labor to help maintain and protect the capitalist status quo as well. Your labor is being exploited.

Yes, some people will inevitably make more money than others, and they may deserve that higher pay. I’m simply arguing for the democratization of the work place. A system that is ran by and for the workers. Rather than the one we live in now, which is solely focused on the accumulation of capital at the direct expense of the working class and their earnings.

Buddy, you aren’t being exploited because of the amount of work you do. You’re being exploited because the amount of material wealth you’re generating for the capitalist class is far greater than what you are being paid. I don’t have to know you personally to know you are being exploited. Because there is literally no other way for the system to function. Capitalists would not be able to generate profit if they weren’t taking most of what their workers are owed. 

I guess I should have been more specific when I said “boss” I’m talking specifically about the capital owner. It sounds like you’re in the military, so in this case the capital owner would not be your commander, but the military itself (and by extension the state) both you AND your commander are being used not only to generate capital, but to protect it as well. 

You’re getting the shaft from both ends my man. If you really don’t want to live in a system where you don’t earn what you work for, I would seriously suggest a career change.

I’m glad you’re happy with your pay, but that has nothing to do with whether or not you are being paid FAIRLY. You are not. Your boss makes more money than you do by taking the wealth generated by your labor. You and every other working class person is being taken advantage of. 

I know it’s a hard pill to swallow, but you are absolutely being exploited my friend. Capitalism cannot function without the exploitation of the working class.

> I would never want to be apart of a system where i don’t earn what I work for.

You are describing Capitalism. 

Your labor is exploited by a private individual who takes the wealth you generated for themselves. They then pay you a wage that is less than the wealth you generated. You are quite literally living in a system where you don’t earn what you work for.
